approvalRequirements: Applicant must have an active Benton PUD electric account for the home site.
The manufactured home must be ENERGY STAR or NEEM certified, electrically heated, and located in Benton PUD service territory.
A complete application must be submitted within six months of purchase with the Certificate of Compliance and required purchase and site documentation.
Program funding must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The rebate is formulaic and paid after a complete qualifying application is processed; funding exhaustion and document validation are the main residual risks.
reviews.evidenceText: Benton PUD currently offers $1,200 to $1,400 for qualifying ENERGY STAR manufactured homes. Electric heat, service-territory location, filing within six months, and a compliance certificate are required, and the program continues until funding expires.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Benton PUD commercial, industrial, or agricultural electric customer.
The project must receive the required pre-installation assessment and written authorization before equipment is purchased or work begins.
Installed equipment must meet the approved measure specifications and program cost-effectiveness requirements.
Applicant must submit the program application, tax form, calculations or certification documents, itemized invoices, and product specifications.
The project must pass any required post-installation verification or inspection and remain within available program funding and incentive limits.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Projects that receive written authorization, install the approved qualifying scope, and pass final documentation and inspection checks are ordinarily paid, subject to funding and program limits.
reviews.evidenceText: Benton PUD requires business projects to begin with an energy assessment and written authorization. Payment follows installation, complete supporting records, and successful post-installation verification; incentive limits and available funds apply.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a qualifying Benton PUD residential electric customer and meet the measure-specific heating or service requirements.
Equipment and installation must meet current program efficiency specifications and use an approved contractor where required.
The customer or participating contractor must submit the applicable rebate application with itemized invoices, model and serial information, and required efficiency certifications.
The installation must pass any requested verification or inspection and program funding must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current residential rebates use objective equipment and documentation rules, and qualifying contractor-submitted or customer-submitted claims are generally paid after review while funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Benton PUD lists current residential equipment, HVAC, weatherization, water-heating, appliance, and EV-related rebates. Measure-specific efficiency, contractor, invoice, certification, and inspection rules apply, and offers remain subject to available funding.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Berkeley Electric Cooperative member, generally with at least twelve months of membership history.
The home must complete the required building-performance assessment and the proposed improvements must meet program savings and payback criteria.
Applicant must pass credit underwriting and execute the required financing and security documents.
Work must be completed by an approved contractor and pass post-installation inspection and member signoff before contractor payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Approval depends on credit underwriting, the audit and payback screen, approved scope and contractor, and execution of secured financing documents, so an eligible project is not routinely assured financing.
reviews.evidenceText: The HomeAdvantage program currently offers member financing for approved efficiency work, but requires a home assessment, acceptable project economics, credit review, approved contractors, closing documents, and final inspection before funds are released.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a Berkeley Electric Cooperative member at the qualifying residence.
The installed HVAC system or enrolled thermostat must be an eligible current-program product and satisfy the applicable technical requirements.
Applicant must complete the current rebate or enrollment process and provide requested purchase, installation, account, and equipment records.
Household or equipment limits must be observed, and annual thermostat credits require continued qualifying event participation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current incentives rely primarily on objective membership, equipment, installation, and enrollment checks, so compliant claims or enrollments are normally approved.
reviews.evidenceText: Berkeley Electric currently publishes smart-thermostat incentives and dual-fuel heating rebates for members. Payment or annual bill credits depend on qualifying equipment, completed enrollment or application, applicable household limits, and continued event participation for thermostat credits.

approvalRequirements: The property owner or authorized representative must own a renewable energy system that qualifies under the Wisconsin statutory exemption.
The exemption request must be filed with the local assessor on the current Department of Revenue form by March 1 of the assessment year.
The filing must include the requested system description, manufacturer, capacity, operating information, and supporting records.
The local assessor must determine that the property falls within the statutory exemption.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The exemption is statutory and generally follows a timely, documented qualifying filing, although the local assessor must validate the system and stand-alone battery storage is not established as eligible by the cited law or form.
reviews.evidenceText: Wisconsin requires Form PR-303 to be filed with the local assessor by March 1 for qualifying solar, wind, biogas, or synthetic-gas energy systems. The current statutory text and form do not establish a separate exemption for stand-alone battery storage.

approvalRequirements: The taxpayer must acquire or use equipment or biomass material specifically covered by the statutory compensating-tax deduction.
The equipment or material must be used for a qualifying biomass energy purpose described in the statute.
The deduction must be claimed on the applicable New Mexico tax return for a transaction occurring before the statutory July 1, 2027 sunset.
The taxpayer must retain records sufficient to substantiate the qualifying property, use, value, and timing if reviewed or audited.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: This is a statutory return deduction rather than a discretionary award; a properly documented qualifying claim should generally be allowed, subject to normal tax review and the sunset date.
reviews.evidenceText: New Mexico law permits a compensating-tax deduction for listed biomass equipment and materials used for qualifying biomass energy activities before July 1, 2027. The benefit is claimed through tax reporting rather than a separate advance program approval.

approvalRequirements: The installed property must meet the statutory definition of an eligible biomass gasification system or methane digester system.
After construction, the owner must apply to the local tax-collecting unit with the required system and ownership information.
For a methane digester, the owner must obtain the required agricultural, environmental, and compliance certifications and satisfy ongoing operating conditions.
The owner must submit required periodic affidavits and permit inspections or other statutory verification.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The exemption is statutory once the system and required certifications are established, but local review and measure-specific agency certifications create meaningful compliance gates.
reviews.evidenceText: Michigan law exempts qualifying biomass gasification and certified methane-digester property. The owner must apply through the local property-tax process, and methane digesters are subject to specified agency certifications, operating conditions, and periodic verification.

approvalRequirements: The transaction must involve qualifying biomass material used to produce energy, electricity, or steam for a qualifying subsequent sale or use under Georgia law.
Fossil fuels and nonqualifying materials or uses must be excluded.
The purchaser must obtain and provide the Georgia Department of Revenue authorization or exemption documentation required for the transaction.
The taxpayer must retain invoices and records supporting the material type, use, and exempt treatment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The exemption is statutory and should be routinely recognized after the Department of Revenue verifies the qualifying biomass-material use, but it does not establish an exemption for the biomass equipment purchase itself.
reviews.evidenceText: Georgia's current exemption listing covers qualifying biomass material used to produce energy, electricity, or steam that is subsequently sold and identifies a Department of Revenue Letter of Authorization as documentation. The cited exemption concerns biomass material, not general equipment acquisition.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a qualifying Black Hills Energy commercial or industrial electric customer in the covered South Dakota or Weston County service area.
New equipment must meet the current measure-specific efficiency and installation requirements.
Custom projects and studies must receive any required preapproval before purchase or installation; prescriptive measures must follow their applicable process.
Applicant must submit the current application with itemized invoices, specifications, calculations, and certifications by the program deadline.
The project must pass cost-effectiveness and verification requirements and program funds must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Prescriptive measures are generally paid after objective eligibility and documentation review, while custom measures add preapproval and cost-effectiveness gates; limited first-come funding remains the principal uncertainty.
reviews.evidenceText: Black Hills Energy's 2026 commercial program covers qualifying electric customers and prescriptive efficiency measures, with separate preapproval rules for custom work. Complete invoices and technical records are required, and applications are subject to cost-effectiveness review, deadlines, limits, and available funds.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a current Black Hills Energy Colorado electric customer in good standing and, for the residential offer, drive an eligible electric or plug-in hybrid vehicle.
The customer must purchase an eligible new Level 2 charger and have it installed by a licensed electrician at the served location in compliance with permits and codes.
The customer must enroll in the required time-of-day or approved managed-charging arrangement and accept the program terms.
A complete 2026 application with receipts, equipment information, installation records, and any requested validation data must be submitted by the deadline.
Program funds must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The rebate uses objective customer, charger, installation, and rate-enrollment conditions, so a complete compliant claim is ordinarily approved while limited funds remain.
reviews.evidenceText: Ready EV currently requires Black Hills electric service, an approved charger, licensed installation at the served site, and participation in the specified time-of-day arrangement. The 2026 residential form requires a complete post-installation claim and states that funds are limited.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a current Black Hills Energy residential electric customer in South Dakota or the covered Weston County, Wyoming, service area.
New equipment must meet the published 2026 efficiency and installation specifications.
The customer must submit the applicable application with an itemized invoice, model and serial information, installation date, and required efficiency certification.
Installation and application must occur within the current program dates and funding must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program is a prescriptive rebate with objective equipment and documentation checks, making approval likely for a timely complete claim while the limited budget remains open.
reviews.evidenceText: Black Hills Energy currently lists residential electric rebates for South Dakota and Weston County, including qualifying smart thermostats, heat pumps, cooling equipment, and heat-pump water heaters. The 2026 process requires qualifying equipment, invoices and certifications, timely filing, and available funds.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must identify the exact Black Hills Energy Wyoming electric or gas service territory and verify that the requested measure is currently offered there.
The customer and installation must satisfy the applicable current program's account, equipment, contractor, code, and documentation requirements.
Any required application, preapproval, invoice, certification, or inspection must be completed under the territory-specific current form.
For active rebate components, funding and measure limits must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The historical statewide record is broader than current availability: 2026 standard efficiency rebates are postponed in Wyoming Gas LLC and Cheyenne Electric territories, while Weston County electric and certain EV-charger incentives remain available.
reviews.evidenceText: Current Black Hills pages show materially different Wyoming availability by territory. Standard 2026 efficiency and demand-side-management rebates are postponed for Wyoming Gas LLC and Cheyenne Electric, although Cheyenne still lists an EV-charger offer and Weston County participates in the South Dakota electric rebate program.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be an active Black Hills Energy electric customer at the proposed southern Colorado installation site.
The proposed new solar system must meet program sizing, equipment, design, interconnection, code, permit, and inspection requirements.
Applicant must submit the required reservation and interconnection materials and receive written approval before installation begins.
Performance-based projects must install required production metering and complete the certificate-of-completion process.
Applicable quarterly program capacity and incentive funding must be available; paired storage must satisfy the current storage rules.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: A written reservation and interconnection approval are required before work, and incentive capacity is allocated under program limits, so technically eligible projects are not assured an incentive reservation.
reviews.evidenceText: Black Hills Energy's Colorado solar program requires an active served site, compliant system sizing and equipment, design and interconnection review, permits, inspection, and written reservation approval before installation. Performance-based incentives require production metering and remain subject to program capacity.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Black Hills Energy Colorado commercial electric customer at the installation site.
New equipment must meet the current prescriptive or custom measure requirements.
Custom projects and studies must receive required preapproval before purchase or installation; prescriptive claims must follow the applicable post-installation process.
Applicant must submit the current form with itemized invoices, specifications, certifications, and calculations.
The project must pass any inspection, verification, and cost-effectiveness review, and funds must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Most listed prescriptive measures are paid after objective documentation review, while custom measures add preapproval and cost-effectiveness checks; limited funds prevent a near-guarantee.
reviews.evidenceText: The 2026 Colorado electric commercial program lists prescriptive lighting, HVAC, refrigeration, motor, drive, and related measures, with custom projects handled separately. Complete invoices and technical records are required, custom work may require advance approval, and payments remain subject to verification and available funds.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a current Black Hills Energy Colorado residential electric customer at the installation address.
The measure must be purchased and installed within the 2026 program period and meet current qualifying-equipment and conditioned-space rules.
A complete application must include itemized invoices, required AHRI or ENERGY STAR documentation, and contractor certification where applicable.
The installation must pass any requested verification or inspection, and funds must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program uses published prescriptive equipment and documentation criteria, so timely complete claims are normally approved, subject to first-come limited funding and verification.
reviews.evidenceText: Black Hills Energy's 2026 Colorado electric residential application requires current electric service, qualifying new equipment installed during the program year, itemized invoices and efficiency documentation, and permits verification or inspection. Applications are processed while limited funds remain.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a current Black Hills Energy Colorado residential natural-gas customer at the installation address.
New qualifying equipment must be installed in an eligible heated living space during the 2026 program period and meet the published efficiency requirements.
For applicable heating measures, Black Hills Energy natural gas must be the home's primary heating fuel.
A complete application must include an itemized contractor invoice, model and serial information, installation date, and required AHRI or ENERGY STAR documentation.
Any requested verification must be completed and program funds must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The current gas rebates are prescriptive and generally paid after objective customer, equipment, fuel, and documentation checks, with limited first-come funding as the main uncertainty.
reviews.evidenceText: The 2026 Colorado gas residential program requires current Black Hills gas service, qualifying equipment in heated living space, itemized installation records, and applicable efficiency certifications. Heating incentives also depend on the utility being the primary heating-fuel provider, and funds are limited.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a current Black Hills Energy Iowa residential natural-gas customer.
New equipment or envelope work must be purchased and installed during the 2026 program year in an eligible heated living space and meet current specifications.
For applicable space-heating measures, Black Hills Energy natural gas must be the primary heating fuel.
The claim must be received within forty-five days of the dealer invoice or by the final program deadline, whichever occurs first.
Applicant must submit an itemized invoice and required efficiency certifications, and funds must remain available.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The program applies objective customer, equipment, fuel, timing, and documentation rules; compliant timely claims are ordinarily approved while the first-come budget remains available.
reviews.evidenceText: Black Hills Energy's 2026 Iowa residential gas form requires current gas service, qualifying work installed during 2026, heated-space and primary-fuel conditions where applicable, itemized invoices and certifications, and filing within forty-five days or the stated final deadline. Funds are limited.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a qualifying Blooming Prairie Public Utilities business electric customer at the project site.
The measure must qualify under the applicable 2026 business rebate form and meet current efficiency, installation, and quantity requirements.
Applicant must obtain measure-specific preapproval or inspection when the applicable form requires it.
A complete claim must include the current application, itemized invoices, equipment specifications, and any required calculations or certifications.
Program limits and available funds must permit payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The municipal program publishes current measure-specific business forms and objective qualification rules, so complete compliant claims are generally paid, subject to any preapproval condition and program limits.
reviews.evidenceText: The current Blooming Prairie member page provides 2026 business rebate forms for lighting, HVAC, drives, refrigeration and food service, controls, compressed air, and custom projects. Each measure follows its form-specific application, documentation, and any preapproval requirements.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a qualifying Blooming Prairie Public Utilities residential electric customer.
The purchased and installed product must be listed in the applicable 2026 residential rebate materials and meet current efficiency and installation requirements.
Applicant must submit the current application with proof of purchase, model information, installation records, and any required certification.
Applicable household, equipment, cost, and funding limits must be satisfied.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Current residential rebates use published product and documentation rules, so a complete qualifying claim is normally approved within program and funding limits.
reviews.evidenceText: Blooming Prairie's current member page links 2026 residential rebate materials for ENERGY STAR products, HVAC and heat pumps, water heating, EV charging, pumps, and related measures. Approval depends on the applicable form, qualifying equipment, and complete purchase and installation records.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be an eligible Blue Grass Energy residential member with an electrically heated home.
Weatherization work must receive the required cooperative review before work and complete the specified pre- and post-project energy evaluations.
HVAC equipment must meet current program efficiency, replacement, installation, and contractor requirements.
The member or contractor must submit the required application, invoices, equipment certification, and verification records.
The measure must comply with current incentive limits and available program funding.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The incentives are prescriptive once the home's electric-heating status, required pre-review, equipment specifications, and final documentation are satisfied; they are not described as competitively ranked awards.
reviews.evidenceText: Blue Grass Energy currently lists Button-Up weatherization and qualifying heat-pump incentives for electrically heated homes. Weatherization requires cooperative contact and energy reviews around the work, while HVAC rebates require published efficiency and installation documentation.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a qualified Blue Ridge Electric Cooperative member and owner of the served property under the current loan rules.
Applicant must submit a complete credit application and receive written credit approval before financing or installation proceeds.
The proposed heat-pump system must meet the current minimum efficiency requirements and be quoted and installed by an approved dealer.
Applicant must execute the loan and security documents, including any required filing, and permit cooperative inspection before contractor payment.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: Financing depends on credit underwriting, property and membership eligibility, equipment approval, security documents, and inspection, so approval cannot be treated as routine even for a technically qualifying heat pump.
reviews.evidenceText: Blue Ridge Electric currently offers member heat-pump financing through approved dealers. The application requires credit approval before the project, qualifying equipment, ownership and membership information, executed financing and security documents, and final inspection before payment.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must have qualifying Blue Ridge Mountain EMC electric service in the applicant's name and own the financed property.
Applicant must submit a complete financing application, authorize credit review, and receive approval before installation.
The heat-pump system must meet program requirements and be installed by a participating qualified contractor.
Applicant must execute any required lien or security documents and permit cooperative inspection after installation.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The offer is loan financing rather than an automatic rebate and remains contingent on credit, property ownership, account status, contractor qualification, security documentation, and inspection.
reviews.evidenceText: Blue Ridge Mountain EMC currently advertises no-money-down heat-pump financing through qualified contractors. The financing application requires eligible service and property ownership, credit authorization and approval, security documentation, and utility inspection after installation.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a Boulder County resident with household income at or below 100 percent of area median income or qualifying program participation.
Income eligibility and the proposed project must receive EnergySmart preapproval before any purchase or work begins.
The project must be a currently eligible 2026 efficiency or electrification measure and meet equipment, contractor, testing, permit, and code requirements.
Work must be completed and invoiced during 2026, and the applicant must submit the claim form with invoices, photos, specifications, certifications, and other required records.
The rebate must remain within the percentage and annual caps, combined-incentive rules, first-come funding, and inspection conditions.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: For a resident who passes income and project preapproval, the current rebate is governed by objective completion and documentation rules; first-come limited funding and final claim verification remain the main risks.
reviews.evidenceText: Boulder County has discontinued its former standard rebates and now offers 2026 county rebates only through the income-qualified program. Eligible residents can receive 50 percent of qualifying project cost up to $2,000 per year after mandatory preapproval, timely completion, complete documentation, and final claim approval while funds remain.

approvalRequirements: Applicant must be a qualifying Brainerd Public Utilities residential customer for the installation or purchase site.
The product or measure must appear on the current 2026 rebate list and meet the stated qualification and installation requirements.
Applicant must submit the current residential rebate application with proof of purchase, model and installation information, and any requested efficiency documentation.
The claim must comply with applicable quantity, cost, account-credit, and program-change conditions.
reviews.awardLikelihoodReason: The 2026 list specifies fixed or formulaic rebates for qualifying equipment, so complete claims are normally approved, although the utility reserves the right to change or withdraw the offer.
reviews.evidenceText: Brainerd Public Utilities publishes a 2026 residential rebate list covering ENERGY STAR appliances, LEDs and controls, cooling and heat pumps, thermostats, heat-pump water heaters, motors, and related measures. Claims require the residential application and supporting purchase or installation records, and the utility may change or withdraw the offer.
